contract: A hub is a hive, not a star. Five frame kinds belong to the mesh and a client may subscribe to all of them. query and cascade are the client's own request/response traffic and ask() owns them, so subscribing to one must be refused rather than silently never firing. A mesh frame is nested: the hub reads message.payload as a HiveMessage of its own and re-stamps the route on it before forwarding, so a flat frame loses the route.

grants.broadcast: admin standing and can_broadcast; a hub disconnects a client that lacks either, it does not answer with an error
grants.propagate: can_propagate, on by default and revocable
grants.escalate: can_escalate, on by default and revocable
grants.note: a hub's HELLO carries its public key, peer name and node id, and nothing about what the client may do, so no client can check before sending

cases.name: the client's own query traffic is refused
the client's own cascade traffic is refused
a bus subscription is not a hive subscription
a misspelled kind is refused rather than never firing
hello is refused: a handshake is the hub's business, not a subscription
shake is refused: a handshake is the hub's business, not a subscription
binary is refused: binary frames arrive through on_binary, which carries the payload type
